claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA is single-phase BCC.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has high density.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has insufficient room-temperature ductility and exhibits brittle failure under compression.
Adding a minor amount of Al to Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will induce B2 precipitation.
The precipitated B2 phase will be ordered and Al-rich.
The B2 phase will form a continuous or semi-continuous reticulated network along grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
Solutionizing followed by aging can promote B2 nucleation and growth.
The Al-modified alloy will have more than 20% higher room-temperature compressive yield strength than the baseline.
The Al-modified alloy will maintain or improve compressive ductility relative to the baseline, with fracture strain above 5%.
A sufficiently fine B2 network will act as a crack deflector rather than a crack initiator.
The B2 network will force cracks to deflect and twist, thereby pinning or arresting them.
Ordered B2 precipitates will provide precipitation hardening.
A continuous reticulated B2 topology will mitigate the brittleness normally associated with continuous brittle phases.
The alloy density will increase slightly after adding Al.
Al addition tends to reduce density because Al is lighter than Hf and Zr.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix can produce high strength but low room-temperature compressive fracture strain.
Excess Al may make the B2 phase continuous and brittle, eliminating the ductility benefit.
Condition 3 of PMC5995863 had a continuous disordered BCC matrix containing discrete approximately 50 nm B2 precipitates.
The operating regime is room-temperature uniaxial compression at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
A continuous B2 matrix giving fracture strain below 1% would be similar to Condition 1 of PMC5995863.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says density will increase slightly, while the uncertainty section says Al addition reduces density. No compositional or volumetric calculation resolves these opposing directions.

The desired mediator is described as continuous or semi-continuous B2, and the mechanism claims this continuity mitigates brittleness, whereas the boundary states that continuous B2 is a brittle crack path. The distinction between a beneficial reticulated network and a harmful continuous matrix is not operationally defined.
The falsification rule characterizes fracture strain below 1% as similar to cited Condition 1, but the cited record reports 4.7% compressive fracture strain for Condition 1.
